title: Fibre-generic locus of a flat finitely presented morphism is stable under generalization
statement: Let $V$ be a valuation ring: an integral domain with fraction field $K$ such that, for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a\in V$ or $a^{-1}\in V$. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat finitely presented morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Here finitely presented means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For $s\in S$ let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $G_f\subseteq |X|$ be the union, over $s\in S$, of the images of the generic points of the irreducible components of $X_s$ [def-weil-irreducible-components]; a generic point of a closed irreducible subset is a point whose closure is that subset. If $x\in G_f$ and $x\in\overline{\{x^{\prime}\}}$ in $X$, then $x^{\prime}\in G_f$.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.3, printed pp. 20--21. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $X$ containing $x$; it also contains $x'$, since opens contain generalizations. Finite presentation implies local finite type directly from the finite polynomial presentations. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $B$ is a finite type $V$-algebra. Write $\mathfrak q'\subseteq\mathfrak q$ for the primes representing $x',x$, and $\mathfrak p'=\mathfrak q'\cap V\subseteq\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap V$. Here the inclusions follow from $\overline{\{\mathfrak a\}}=V(\mathfrak a)$ in a spectrum. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-chart-base-change-iso], the fibre of $U$ at $\mathfrak t$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_V\kappa(\mathfrak t))$. The quotient and localization prime correspondences identify its primes, preserving inclusions, with the primes of $B$ contracting to $\mathfrak t$. Indeed its ring is $(V\setminus\mathfrak t)^{-1}(B/\mathfrak tB)$; the two maps send $(b\bmod\mathfrak tB)/s$ to $b\otimes(1/s)$ and $b\otimes(\bar a/\bar s)$ to $ab/s$.

source.place: Q16 affine reduction; Tag 00QK setup, using localization and quotient prime correspondences

proof.text: Being a generic point of an irreducible component can be checked in any open neighbourhood of the point. In fact, if $C=\overline{\{z\}}$ and an irreducible closed set $H$ strictly contains $C$, then $H\cap U$ is irreducible and strictly contains $C\cap U$: the nonempty open $H\cap U$ is dense in $H$, so containment in the closed set $C$ would force $H\subseteq C$. Conversely, a larger irreducible closed set in $U$ has irreducible closure in the whole space. In a spectrum the correspondence between primes and irreducible closed sets reverses inclusion; thus component-generic points are exactly minimal primes. Consequently $\mathfrak q$ is minimal among the primes over $\mathfrak p$. Suppose for contradiction that $x'$ is not fibre-generic. The correspondence in step 1 then supplies a prime $\mathfrak r\subsetneq\mathfrak q'$ of $B$ with $\mathfrak r\cap V=\mathfrak p'$.

source.place: Q16 elementary open-locality argument; Tag 00KE (definition-Krull), prime/irreducible-closed correspondence

proof.text: Set $A=(V/\mathfrak p')_{\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p'}$, $L=\operatorname{Frac}(A)=\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, and $k=A/\mathfrak m_A=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. This is a valuation ring. To see this without a rank assumption, in a valuation domain any two nonzero elements divide one another in one direction, by applying its defining property to their ratio. Reducing such a divisibility relation modulo a prime proves the same property for the quotient domain. Localizing a domain with this property preserves it: for nonzero $a/s,b/t$, compare $at$ and $bs$. Its maximal ideal is $(\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p')A$, so the displayed residue and fraction fields are the usual localization/quotient descriptions of those residue fields.

source.place: Q16 elementary quotient/localization calculation for the valuation-ring hypothesis of Tag 00QK

proof.text: For $\mathfrak a\in\{\mathfrak r,\mathfrak q'\}$ put $D_{\mathfrak a}=(V\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}(B/\mathfrak a)$. Since $\mathfrak a\cap V=\mathfrak p'$, $D_{\mathfrak a}$ is a domain containing $A$ injectively: all denominators are nonzero, and the injection $V/\mathfrak p'\hookrightarrow B/\mathfrak a$ remains injective after localization. It is finite type over $A$, generated by the images of the finitely many generators of $B$ over $V$. Write $F_{\mathfrak a}=D_{\mathfrak a}\otimes_Ak$ and $E_{\mathfrak a}=D_{\mathfrak a}\otimes_AL$. Explicitly $F_{\mathfrak a}\cong(V\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}(B/(\mathfrak a+\mathfrak pB))$: $\bar b/s\otimes\bar a/\bar t$ maps to $ab/(st)$, with inverse $\bar b/s\mapsto(\bar b/s)\otimes1$. These formulas respect the bilinearity and quotient relations and are inverse on their generators. Likewise [lem-weil-pbc-generic-fibre-localization-domain-irreducible] identifies $E_{\mathfrak a}$ with $(V\setminus\mathfrak p')^{-1}(B/\mathfrak a)$, a nonzero domain. Each $E_{\mathfrak a}$ is finite type over the field $L$, with the same generating images.

source.place: Q16 explicit rings to which Tag 00QK is applied; generic fibres are localizations

proof.text: The quotient description of $F_{\mathfrak a}$ and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus] identify $\operatorname{Spec}F_{\mathfrak a}$ with the closed subset of $U_{\mathfrak p}$ cut out by the images of $\mathfrak a$. It contains $x$, because $\mathfrak a\subseteq\mathfrak q$. In particular $F_{\mathfrak a}\ne0$. Let $C=\overline{\{x\}}$ in $U_{\mathfrak p}$; it is an irreducible component by the hypothesis and step 2. Every closed subset containing $x$ contains $C$. Moreover $C$ is an irreducible component of each $\operatorname{Spec}F_{\mathfrak a}$: any irreducible subset of that closed subset strictly containing $C$ would contradict the maximality of $C$ in $U_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Q16 closed-subset/component argument from the quotient description; Tag 00QK nonzero-special-fibre hypothesis

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-domain-fibre-dimensions] to both $A\subset D_{\mathfrak r}$ and $A\subset D_{\mathfrak q'}$. Step 3 supplies the valuation ring; step 4 supplies the finite type domains containing it; step 5 supplies nonzero special fibres and the common irreducible component $C$. Its equidimensionality clause gives $\dim E_{\mathfrak r}=\dim C=\dim E_{\mathfrak q'}$. These dimensions are finite nonnegative integers by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-trdeg], since the two $E$'s are nonzero finite type domains over $L$. Denote the common dimension by $d$.

source.place: Tag 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), including equidimensionality; finite dimension of finite type field domains

proof.text: Under the localization description in step 4, the quotient $B/\mathfrak r\to B/\mathfrak q'$ induces $E_{\mathfrak r}\twoheadrightarrow E_{\mathfrak q'}$, with prime kernel $I=(V\setminus\mathfrak p')^{-1}(\mathfrak q'/\mathfrak r)$. The quotient identification follows directly by sending the class of $\bar b/s$ modulo $I$ to $(b\bmod\mathfrak q')/s$, with inverse given by the same fraction. The localization prime correspondence shows $I\ne(0)$: the distinct primes $(0)$ and $\mathfrak q'/\mathfrak r$ of $B/\mathfrak r$ both avoid the images of $V\setminus\mathfrak p'$, so their extensions remain distinct. Thus $E_{\mathfrak q'}\cong E_{\mathfrak r}/I$ with $I$ a nonzero prime.

source.place: Q16 fraction calculation and localization prime bijection for the two generic fibres

proof.text: As $E_{\mathfrak q'}$ has finite dimension $d$, there is a prime chain of length $d$ in it: a nonempty set of nonnegative integers with finite supremum has that supremum as maximum. Lift this chain through $E_{\mathfrak r}\twoheadrightarrow E_{\mathfrak q'}$ using [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus]. All its primes contain the nonzero ideal $I$. Prepending the prime $(0)$ of the domain $E_{\mathfrak r}$ gives a strict prime chain of length $d+1$, contradicting $\dim E_{\mathfrak r}=d$. Hence the prime $\mathfrak r$ posited in step 2 cannot exist, and $x'$ is fibre-generic. This proves the assertion, also when $x'=x$ or $\mathfrak p'=\mathfrak p$. Empty fibres contribute no points to $G_f$.

proof_origin.place: Q16 proof using Tag 00QK, replacing the invalid general-base dimension-drop argument in Temkin Lemma 3.5.3
